thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: P2 - routing anomaly detected in smart-routing. Sudden spike in model-variant mismatches and cache-key misses originating from us-west-2. Error rate up 7x for model 'llama-3-redwood/v1' fallback -> variant 'llama-3-quant-stable'. Paging on-call.
jordan: seeing it on the dashboard. traces show a lot of requests routed to the fallback pool; the KV cache returns entries for a different variant (model+region key mismatch). 😬
maria_oncall: I'm paged, joining. any customer-facing errors yet? can you post SLO impact numbers?
sam_ml: metric snippets:
```
- 01:02:14: request_err_rate: 0.02 -> 0.14 (7x)
- 01:02:30: variant_mismatch_rate: 0.005 -> 0.08
- kv_cache_hit_rate (region+model key): 0.93 -> 0.51
```
sam_ml: I think the cache key generator started including the route variant id for some requests but not others — so two requests that should've hit the same prefix are being treated as distinct, causing both incorrect reuse and unexpected misses.
kevin: any recent deploys to smart-routing or the prefixing logic? eng-runtime pushed something last night?
jordan: eng-runtime had a small refactor merging `route_priority` into `route_key` on 1923340000. Might be related.
andrea_prod: increasing customer error noise in support. I posted an incident banner for affected tenants (region=us-west-2, models=llama-3*). initially two enterprise customers reported degraded responses.
maria_oncall: ok mitigation plan — short term: rollback route_key change in host pool for us-west-2 OR flush affected cache prefixes for the variant mapping. Which is less risky?
kevin: flushing prefixes first is lower blast radius. we can target prefixes: `model:llama-3-redwood:v1:us-west-2:*` and `variant:llama-3-quant-stable:us-west-2:*` to clear inconsistency, then observe.
jordan: commands to flush (run from ops-private):
```
# Dry-run: list keys
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  "https://kv-control.us-west-2.redwood.internal/keys?prefix=model:llama-3-redwood:v1:us-west-2"

# Flush keys
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  "https://kv-control.us-west-2.redwood.internal/flush" \
  -d '{"prefix":"model:llama-3-redwood:v1:us-west-2"}'
```
maria_oncall: I'll run the dry-run and then flush; will monitor errors and hit-rate. I'll also incrementally roll the rollback if flush doesn't help.
incident-bot: NOTE: Runbook step 3: alert all customers with >5% error increase via cs-notify template. See runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood/internal/kvcache-mismatch
kevin: quick note: don't flush global prefix — only region+model. If the rollback is needed we should coordinate with eng-runtime and schedule a quick canary.
andrea_prod: I muted some support alerts and told CS to escalate only on confirmed data loss. So far it's degraded correctness (wrong variant answers), not data deletion.
jordan: dry-run shows ~12k keys under the model prefix, mostly for the older routing layout.
maria_oncall: starting flush now (01:06:02Z). running in 5k batches.
sam_ml: I'll watch ML evals for quality regressions — if variant A incorrectly served, we'll see sudden eval_score delta for our smoke prompts.
kevin: Maria, if you see any surge in latency post-flush, pause and report. flushing will cause cache misses and cold KV refills.
01:06:35 maria_oncall: flush batch 1 complete (5k keys). error rate down ~20% in the first 30s.
01:07:10 jordan: routing fallback count also dropped ~30% in the last minute.
01:07:45 andrea_prod: CS update: customer A reports responses are back to normal for a sample. thanks.
01:08:05 maria_oncall: flush 2 complete. continuing.
pagerduty-bot: Hand-off scheduled: maria_oncall -> kevin at 02:15 UTC. Use `#oncall-handoff` for formal notes.
02:12:00 kevin: I'm on-call now. what's the current state?
02:12:12 maria_oncall: residual mismatch tail — variant_mismatch_rate at 0.01 (still elevated vs baseline 0.005). Flushed most region/model prefixes; still seeing some mis-routed requests from an older routing cache in a subset of pools.
02:13:00 kevin: I propose a targeted rollback: revert the `route_key` change on the pool router for us-west-2. That will normalize key generation. Preflight: confirm there's a canary without traffic that we can flip first.
02:13:30 jordan: canary ready. I can flip one router instance to old behavior.
02:14:15 kevin: doing canary flip now (02:14:20Z). monitoring.
02:14:50 jordan: canary looks good. no error increase, cache-hit stabilizing.
02:15:10 kevin: rolling out to remaining 3 routers in us-west-2.
02:16:05 sam_ml: evals back to baseline on smoke prompts. nice.
02:16:30 andrea_prod: CS: reaching out to customers impacted with an RCA draft: short summary + mitigation + ask to confirm if they saw incorrect answers. No PII exposed.
02:17:00 maria_oncall: metrics: variant_mismatch_rate 0.003, kv_cache_hit_rate 0.91, request_err_rate back to 0.021 (near baseline)
02:17:45 kevin: follow-ups: 1) revert the `route_key` refactor PR with a fix & unit tests 2) add integration test that asserts stable key composition across route changes 3) add a canary gate to new key-format deploys 4) add an alert to detect sudden divergence between `cache_key_hash` and `route_assignment` per region.
02:18:20 jordan: I'll open the follow-up tickets and assign to eng-runtime + eng-sre.
02:19:00 incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated — routing rollback + targeted flush completed. No active customer-impacting errors remain. Postmortem assignment: maria_oncall -> eng-runtime (owner: jordan). Priority: P2. Timeline window recorded.
02:19:15 pagerduty-bot: Pager duty: mark incident as acknowledged -> resolved in 40 minutes by kevin.
02:20:00 andrea_prod: Thanks team. I'll post a short customer-facing note and link to the postmortem when ready.
kevin: final note: root cause appears to be a deploy that changed the composition of the KV prefix without backward compatibility. It caused a temporary namespace split — both wrong reuse (serving mismatched variants) and misses (cold refills). We'll include compatibility checks in the rollout checklist.
andrea_prod: filing the postmortem draft now. please add any notes/comments in #incidents-postmortems.
jordan: closing thread; follow-ups in tickets. :white_check_mark:
